chapter: Quincy Jones, films and harmonica heroes
title: Stevie Wonder as a harmonica player
summary: He argues Stevie is underrated as a harmonica player and mentions his Giant Steps jam.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, even Stevie Wonder… I mean, he…

Oh, Stevie, yes. He’s the most… Oh, Stevie… He’s not enough considered as a harmonica player. They say, “Oh yeah, he writes every [unintelligible].” He’s a great composer, a showman. He sings [unintelligible]. But I can tell you what he plays… You listen to the YouTube again when he plays… plays Alfie with Burt Bacharach. [inaudible]. I have it on my… but I can’t show it to you. There is no signal here. I [had thought?] that he played… I heard him. He was as a guest sometimes as a… Stanley Clark, the bassist, teaches somewhere at a school or conservatory or university—a jazz class. And Stevie went, and they played. I think in Spain. Giant Steps. He plays the [inaudible] piano.
But he… don’t fool with Stevie.
